current_activity: becoming operational under Patton at Néhou with VIII Corps passing to it
notes: Event date: Breakout-18 p343 (Third Army operational at noon, 1 August, with VIII Corps in the Pontaubault–Avranches area). Event definition: the army becomes operational. Location: local-history sources (KilroyTrip, normandie1944) place Patton's Third Army headquarters in an orchard at Néhou from 6 July to about 2 August 1944, so the headquarters was at Néhou on 1 August; the Green Book does not give the location. Coordinates: OpenStreetMap Nominatim centroid of Néhou (the orchard is not located). Relationship: 12th Army Group assigned (Breakout-18 p343). Previously this row carried an Avranches area point (50 km) because no headquarters location had been found. Batch 2 check: the Néhou memorial text (uswarmemorials.org) says Patton's command post was in the village from 6 July to 2 August 1944, and the CMH command-post list (World War II by Day) puts Third Army at Bricquebec-en-Cotentin, about 8 km away, from 26 July to 1 August with Folligny from 2 August (C0486). The two sources agree on the area and the departure date, so confidence is 0.7; the Néhou centroid is kept.
